rows.quote: Data on stroke patients were obtained from one of the largest genome-wide meta-analyses conducted by the MEGASTROKE Consortium (Table 1) [20].
rows.reference_quote: Malik R Chauhan G Traylor M Sargurupremraj M Okada Y Mishra A Rutten-Jacobs L Giese AK Multiancestry genome-wide association study of 520,000 subjects identifies 32 loci associated with stroke and stroke subtypes Nat Genet 2018 50 4 524 537 10.1038/s41588-018-0058-3 29531354 PMC5968830
rows.coder_note: Step 2: the sentence attributes the stroke data to the MEGASTROKE Consortium meta-analysis [20]; entry 20 (DOI 10.1038/s41588-018-0058-3, PMID 29531354) is the source of exactly one outcome row. The Table 1 counts are subtype-specific European-subset sizes, which under rule H are not a conflict and identify no other row. No accession (C4 not applicable).

Step 4, rules C, D and I1: 'UK Biobank dataset' with counts alone (3314 cases/357,880 controls) and no phenotype definition, release name, accession or citation; a biobank name with only a number of participants does not identify a release; no accession (C4 not applicable).

Step 4, rules D and F: the row's passages give 'IMPROVE,INTERVAL,KORA F4' in a table with a pooled size (9775) that equals no row's; the grouped citation [17-19] under the MEGASTROKE row's passage names only IMPROVE in its sentence and maps to no single cohort, so rule I2 does not apply; no accession (C4 not applicable).
